title: Context Window Economics: Summarizing vs Truncating Chat History

steps.prompt: An Agentforce service conversation often runs past 40 turns. Every model call replays the full transcript, so prompt tokens per call rise with each turn. Customers often refer back to account details they gave in the first few turns. How should the architect manage the conversation history?

options.label: Keep recent turns verbatim and condense earlier turns into a key-facts summary
options.rationale: Context should be prioritized rather than cut arbitrarily: recent history comes first, and after the first several turns the earlier conversation is summarized so critical facts persist without growing the token budget. The early account details stay available while each call stops getting larger.

options.label: Send only the ten most recent turns and drop older ones from each call
options.rationale: A fixed window drops the account details customers gave in the first turns, so the agent has to ask for them again when customers refer back.

options.label: Move to a model with a larger context window so the full transcript fits
options.rationale: A larger window lets the transcript fit, but every call still pays for the full history, so prompt tokens and cost keep rising with each turn.
